title: Matrices move the plane
objectives: Recognise rotations, stretches and shears from their matrices.

screens.title: Where do the arrows go?
screens.prose: A matrix moves every point of the plane: $\mathbf{x}$ goes to $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$. Take $\mathbf{A} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.
screens.question: Drag $\mathbf{e}_1 = (1, 0)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2 = (0, 1)$ to where $\mathbf{A}$ sends them.

hints.text: Last lesson: $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{e}_1$ is one of column 1 and none of column 2.
$\mathbf{A}\mathbf{e}_1$ is column 1 and $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{e}_2$ is column 2.
Put $\mathbf{e}_1$ on $(2, 1)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ on $(-1, 1)$.

feedback.correct: $\mathbf{e}_1$ goes to column 1, $(2, 1)$, and $\mathbf{e}_2$ to column 2, $(-1, 1)$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{e}_1$ is the first column of $\mathbf{A}$, and $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{e}_2$ the second.

byKey.row1: An arrow sits on $(2, -1)$, the first **row**. The image of $\mathbf{e}_1$ is the first column, $(2, 1)$.
byKey.row2: An arrow sits on $(1, 1)$, the second **row**. The image of $\mathbf{e}_2$ is the second column, $(-1, 1)$.
byKey.e1: $\mathbf{e}_1$ is not there yet. It goes to column 1, $(2, 1)$.
byKey.e2: $\mathbf{e}_2$ is not there yet. It goes to column 2, $(-1, 1)$.

explain.text: You moved $\mathbf{e}_1$ to column 1 and $\mathbf{e}_2$ to column 2. The rest of the grid follows them: every unit square becomes the same parallelogram.

screens.title: A turn of the plane
screens.prose: This matrix $\mathbf{R}$ turns the plane anticlockwise by the angle on the slider. The dashed square is where the unit square started. The caption shows $\mathbf{R}$, rounded.
screens.question: Set the angle to 90°. Which matrix turns the plane a quarter turn?

options.why: That reads the images as rows. Its columns send $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(0, -1)$: a quarter turn clockwise.
That sends $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(-1, 0)$: a half turn, 180°.

hints.text: At 90°, where does the arrow $\mathbf{R}\mathbf{e}_1$ point?
At 90°, $\mathbf{e}_1$ points straight up, to $(0, 1)$. That is column 1.
$\mathbf{e}_1 \to (0, 1)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2 \to (-1, 0)$. Write them as the columns.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. At 90°, read where $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ land, and make those the columns.

explain.text: At 90° the turn sends $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(0, 1)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(-1, 0)$. Those images are the columns, so the quarter turn is $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$.

screens.title: Any angle
screens.prose: Moving the plane by a matrix is a **linear transformation**. A turn by $\theta$ sends $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$: one unit along the direction at angle $\theta$.
screens.question: Where does $\mathbf{e}_2$ land?

options.why: That turns $\mathbf{e}_2$ the other way. At $\theta = 90°$ it gives $(1, 0)$, but a quarter turn anticlockwise takes $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(-1, 0)$.
Check $\theta = 0$: nothing moves, so $\mathbf{e}_2$ must stay at $(0, 1)$. This gives $(-1, 0)$.

hints.text: $\mathbf{e}_2$ starts at angle 90° and turns by $\theta$ as well.
Check your answer at $\theta = 0$ and at $\theta = 90°$.
$\mathbf{e}_2$ ends at angle $90° + \theta$: $(\cos(90° + \theta), \sin(90° + \theta))$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check each option at $\theta = 0$ (no move) and $\theta = 90°$ (to $(-1, 0)$).

explain.text: $\mathbf{e}_2$ ends at angle $90° + \theta$, so its coordinates are $\cos(90° + \theta) = -\sin\theta$ and $\sin(90° + \theta) = \cos\theta$. The images are the columns: $$\mathbf{R}(\theta) = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}.$$

screens.title: A shear
screens.prose: $\mathbf{S} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & k \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ keeps $\mathbf{e}_1$ fixed and slides $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(k, 1)$. Move the slider and watch the point $(0, 2)$.
screens.question: With $k = 1.5$, where does $(0, 2)$ go?

hints.text: $\mathbf{S}(0, 2) = 0\,\mathbf{S}\mathbf{e}_1 + 2\,\mathbf{S}\mathbf{e}_2$.
$\mathbf{S}\mathbf{e}_2 = (1.5, 1)$ when $k = 1.5$.

feedback.correct: $2\,(1.5, 1) = (3, 2)$: the point slides 3 across and keeps its height.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Set the slider to 1.5 and read the image, or compute $2\,(k, 1)$.

byKey.r0c1: The point slides sideways by $k$ times its height: $1.5 \times 2 = 3$.
byKey.r1c1: A shear like this never changes the height. The $y$ coordinate stays 2.

explain.text: $\mathbf{S}(0, 2) = 2\,(1.5, 1) = (3, 2)$. Each point slides sideways by $k$ times its height, so points on the $x$-axis do not move. This is a **shear**.

screens.title: A stretch
screens.prose: Another matrix moved the plane. The grid shows where the old grid lines went, and the arrows show where $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ landed.
screens.question: Which matrix $\mathbf{D}$ did this?

options.why: That stretches the vertical direction by 3. Here the horizontal arrow $\mathbf{D}\mathbf{e}_1$ has length 3.
The minus sign would flip $\mathbf{e}_2$ to point down. $\mathbf{D}\mathbf{e}_2$ still points up.

hints.text: Read the two arrows: they are the columns.
$\mathbf{D}\mathbf{e}_1 = (3, 0)$.

feedback.correct: Columns $(3, 0)$ and $(0, 0.5)$: three times wider, half as tall.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read where each arrow ends and write those as the columns.

explain.text: $\mathbf{e}_1$ went to $(3, 0)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(0, 0.5)$. Zeros off the diagonal mean each axis is only scaled. A matrix like this is **diagonal**: a pure stretch along the axes.

screens.title: A swap
screens.prose: $\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. Read its columns before you decide.
screens.question: What does $\mathbf{M}$ do to the plane?

options.text: It reflects the plane in the line $y = x$
It turns the plane a quarter turn
options.why: A quarter turn sends $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(-1, 0)$, with a minus sign. $\mathbf{M}$ sends it to $(1, 0)$.

options.text: It reflects the plane in the $x$-axis
options.why: That keeps $\mathbf{e}_1$ and sends $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(0, -1)$. $\mathbf{M}$ moves $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(0, 1)$.

options.text: Nothing: it only swaps the order of the numbers
options.why: Swapping coordinates moves points: P at $(3, 1)$ goes to $(1, 3)$.

hints.text: Where do $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ go?
$\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_1 = (0, 1)$ and $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_2 = (1, 0)$: they swap.
P at $(3, 1)$ goes to $(1, 3)$. Which line sits halfway between them?

feedback.correct: $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ swap places, so every point is mirrored in $y = x$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_2$, then picture P.

explain.text: $\mathbf{M}$ swaps $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$, so $(x, y)$ goes to $(y, x)$. P at $(3, 1)$ lands on $(1, 3)$, its mirror image in $y = x$.

screens.title: Flattened
screens.prose: $\mathbf{N} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$. Its second column, $(2, 4)$, is twice its first, $(1, 2)$.
screens.question: What happens to the unit square?

options.text: It is flattened onto the line $y = 2x$
It becomes a parallelogram with sides $(1, 2)$ and $(2, 4)$
options.why: Those sides point the same way. A parallelogram whose sides are parallel has no width: it is a line segment.

options.text: It is turned and stretched, but keeps some area
options.why: Every image $x(1, 2) + y(2, 4) = (x + 2y)(1, 2)$ is a multiple of $(1, 2)$. Nothing leaves the line.

hints.text: Every image is $x\,(1, 2) + y\,(2, 4)$.
$(2, 4) = 2\,(1, 2)$, so every image is a multiple of $(1, 2)$.
Multiples of $(1, 2)$ all lie on the line $y = 2x$.

feedback.correct: Both columns lie on $y = 2x$, so every image does too.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write the image of $(x, y)$ as a multiple of $(1, 2)$.

explain.text: $\mathbf{N}(x, y) = (x + 2y)\,(1, 2)$, always on the line $y = 2x$. The whole plane is squashed onto that line, and the square has area 0. No matrix can undo this; level 3 returns to it.

screens.title: Read the columns
screens.prose: Many people read a matrix row by row. Try this one: $\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.
screens.question: Tap the point where $\mathbf{M}$ sends $\mathbf{e}_2 = (0, 1)$.

hints.text: $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_2$ is one of the columns. Which one?
Column 2 of $\mathbf{M}$ reads $(2, 1)$ from top to bottom.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_2$ is the second column, read downwards.

byKey.D: You read row 2, $(0, 1)$, as the image of $\mathbf{e}_2$, so it stayed put. Images are columns: $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_2 = (2, 1)$.
byKey.A: That is row 1, $(1, 2)$. The image of $\mathbf{e}_2$ is column 2, $(2, 1)$.

explain.text: Column 2 of $\mathbf{M}$ is $(2, 1)$, so $\mathbf{e}_2$ slides right to B. Column 1 is $(1, 0)$, so $\mathbf{e}_1$ stays put. $\mathbf{M}$ is a shear with $k = 2$.

screens.title: Columns are images
screens.prose: Every time, you read the picture from the columns. Column $j$ is where $\mathbf{e}_j$ lands, and every other point follows: $$\mathbf{A}\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = x\,\mathbf{A}\mathbf{e}_1 + y\,\mathbf{A}\mathbf{e}_2.$$ So a matrix is fixed by two arrows.
screens.question: Which matrix reflects the plane in the $x$-axis?

options.why: That flips $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(-1, 0)$: a reflection in the $y$-axis.
That swaps the axes: a reflection in $y = x$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. A reflection in the $x$-axis keeps $\mathbf{e}_1$ and flips $\mathbf{e}_2$.

explain.text: Reflecting in the $x$-axis keeps $\mathbf{e}_1$ where it is and sends $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(0, -1)$. Those are the columns.

screens.title: From assets to factors
screens.prose: A desk holds a stock and a bond, with daily returns $s$ and $b$. It reports two factors instead: market $m = \tfrac{1}{2}(s + b)$ and spread $d = s - b$. One matrix $\mathbf{M}$ turns $(s, b)$ into $(m, d)$.

state.caption: Column 1 is $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{e}_1$: the factors on a day when the stock rises 1 and the bond is flat.

screens.question: Fill in $\mathbf{M}$.

hints.text: Column 1 is $(m, d)$ on a day with $s = 1$ and $b = 0$.
With $s = 0, b = 1$: $m = 0.5$ and $d = -1$. That is column 2.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Column 1 is $(m, d)$ for $(s, b) = (1, 0)$; column 2 for $(0, 1)$.

byKey.r1c2: With $s = 0$ and $b = 1$, $d = 0 - 1 = -1$. The bond enters the spread with a minus sign.

explain.text: A pure stock day becomes $(0.5, 1)$ and a pure bond day $(0.5, -1)$. Those are the columns. Today, with $s = 3\%$ and $b = -1\%$, the desk reports $m = 1\%$ and $d = 4\%$.

ideas: A matrix moves the whole plane. Column $j$ is where $\mathbf{e}_j$ lands, and every other point follows.
Rotation $\mathbf{R}(\theta)$, diagonal stretch, shear $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & k \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and reflections are all read off their columns.
If one column is a multiple of the other, the plane is flattened onto a line.
summary.trap: The images of the basis vectors are the columns, not the rows. Reading rows gives the wrong picture.

quiz.prose: A half turn spins the plane 180° about the origin.
quiz.question: Which matrix does it?

options.why: That sends $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(0, 1)$: a quarter turn, 90°.
That keeps $\mathbf{e}_1$ in place: a reflection in the $x$-axis. A half turn reverses both arrows.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. After 180°, where do $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ point?

explain.text: A half turn sends $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(-1, 0)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(0, -1)$. Check with $\mathbf{R}(180°)$: $\cos 180° = -1$ and $\sin 180° = 0$.

options.why: You combined the rows: $1(1, 2) + 1(0, 1)$. Combine the columns $(1, 0)$ and $(2, 1)$.
That is where $\mathbf{e}_2$ goes. $(1, 1)$ also has one of $\mathbf{e}_1$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the two columns.

explain.text: $(1, 1) = \mathbf{e}_1 + \mathbf{e}_2$, so it goes to $(1, 0) + (2, 1) = (3, 1)$. It slides sideways by $2 \times$ its height of 1.

quiz.prose: A matrix sends $\mathbf{e}_1$ to $(0, 2)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$ to $(-1, 0)$.
quiz.question: Which matrix is it?

options.why: You wrote the images as rows. They go in as columns.
You put the image of $\mathbf{e}_2$ first. Column 1 is the image of $\mathbf{e}_1$.

feedback.correct: Columns $(0, 2)$ and $(-1, 0)$: a quarter turn with $\mathbf{e}_1$ stretched to length 2.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write each image as a column, in order.

explain.text: Column 1 is $(0, 2)$ and column 2 is $(-1, 0)$. Compared with the quarter turn, $\mathbf{e}_1$ is also stretched to length 2.

quiz.prose: The desk from the lesson reports market $m = \tfrac{1}{2}(s + b)$ and spread $d = s - b$. Today the stock returned 2% and the bond 4%.
quiz.question: What is the spread factor today?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The spread is the stock return minus the bond return.

byKey.reversed: You took the bond minus the stock. The spread row of the matrix is $(1, -1)$: stock minus bond.
byKey.market: That is the market factor, the average. The spread is the difference.

explain.text: The spread row of $\mathbf{M}$ is $(1, -1)$, so $d = 1 \times 2\% - 1 \times 4\% = -2\%$. The bond beat the stock today.
